notes.title: Combinational logic – revision sheet
notes.md:
## Gates and Boolean algebra
- Basic: AND, OR, NOT; **universal: NAND, NOR**; XOR = A'B + AB' (1 when different); XNOR = equality
- NAND-only XOR needs **4** gates (NOR-only 5); NOT from NAND – join inputs
- Laws: identity (x+0=x, x·1=x), complement, idempotent, **absorption** (x + xy = x, x(x+y) = x), x + x'y = x + y, **De Morgan** ((AB)' = A' + B', (A+B)' = A'B'), duality
- Number of functions of n variables = 2^(2ⁿ)

## K-maps
- Gray order 00 01 11 10; pair eliminates 1 variable, quad 2, octet 3; corners and edges are adjacent
- Σm(1,3,5,7) = C; Σm(0,2,8,10) = B'D'; Σm(0,2,4,6) = C'
- Don't-cares (X) help make larger groups; essential prime implicants; canonical SOP (minterms) / POS (maxterms)
- Variable-entered map: 4 variables with 2 map-entered → 4 cells

## Combinational circuits (no memory, no feedback, no clock)
| Circuit | Key facts |
|---|---|
| Half adder | S = A⊕B, C = AB (2 outputs) |
| Full adder | S = A⊕B⊕Cin, Cout = AB + Cin(A⊕B); = 2 HA + OR |
| Half subtractor | D = A⊕B, Borrow = A'B |
| Ripple adder | delay ∝ n; carry look-ahead is faster |
| BCD adder | add 0110 if sum > 9 |
| Decoder | n → 2ⁿ, one minterm per output; decoder + OR = any function |
| Encoder | 2ⁿ → n; priority encoder |
| MUX | 2ⁿ:1 with n select lines (data selector); 16:1 = 5 × 4:1; 8:1 = 7 × 2:1 |
| DEMUX | 1:2ⁿ (data distributor) |
| Comparator | A>B = AB', A=B = A⊙B, A<B = A'B |
- Binary→Gray: g = b ⊕ (b >> 1) (1011 → 1110); parity – XOR; hazards – add consensus term

notes.title: Sequential logic – revision sheet
notes.md:
## Latches and flip-flops
- Sequential = output depends on inputs + stored state; latch (level) vs flip-flop (edge); bistable multivibrator
- **SR**: NOR latch – S=R=1 invalid; NAND latch – S'=R'=0 invalid; Q+ = S + R'Q (SR = 0)
- **D**: Q+ = D (no invalid state; delay; registers)
- **JK**: Q+ = JQ' + K'Q; 00 hold, 01 reset, 10 set, 11 toggle; race-around when J=K=1 with a long pulse → **master–slave** / edge triggering
- **T**: Q+ = T ⊕ Q; JK→T: J = K = T; JK→D: J = D, K = D'
- J=K=1 → output = clock/2 (frequency divider)
- Excitation: JK 0→1 = (1, X); SR 1→0 = (0, 1); D = Q+
- Preset/clear asynchronous; setup time (before edge), hold time (after edge)
- Mealy (state + input) vs Moore (state only); flip-flops for N states = ⌈log₂ N⌉

## Registers and counters
- Shift registers SISO, SIPO (serial→parallel), PISO, PIPO; left shift ×2; universal 74194
- Ring counter n states; **Johnson 2n** states
- Ripple (asynchronous) – delays add (4 × 10 ns → 25 MHz max); synchronous – common clock
- n-bit counter: 0 … 2ⁿ−1; decade counter resets at 1010; mod-6 resets at 110; mod-N divides frequency by N

## ICs and memory
- SSI < MSI < LSI < VLSI; CMOS low power, ECL fastest, TTL common; fan-in/fan-out, noise margin
- Memory with k address and n data lines = 2ᵏ × n; 1K × 8 → 10 address lines; 64K × 16 → 16 lines, 128 KB
- Chips needed = (total words / chip words) × (total width / chip width)
- SRAM (flip-flops, no refresh) vs DRAM (capacitors, refresh); ROM, PROM, EPROM (UV), EEPROM, Flash
- PLA (AND + OR programmable) vs PAL (AND programmable, OR fixed)

notes.title: Data representation – revision sheet
notes.md:
## Number systems
| Base | Digits | Group of bits |
|---|---|---|
| Binary 2 | 0 1 | – |
| Octal 8 | 0–7 | 3 |
| Decimal 10 | 0–9 | – |
| Hex 16 | 0–9 A–F | 4 |
- Decimal → base r: divide by r, read remainders bottom-up; fractions: multiply by r, read the integer parts top-down (0.625 = 0.101₂)
- Worked: 100 = 144₈ = 64₁₆; 1234 = 4D2₁₆ = 2322₈; F3E₁₆ = 3902; 763.4₈ = 499.5; DAD₁₆ = 3501 = 6655₈

## Complements (r's and (r−1)'s)
- (r−1)'s: subtract each digit from r−1 (9's of 5307 = 4692; 1's = invert bits)
- r's = (r−1)'s + 1 (10's of 2470 = 7530; 2's = invert + 1; shortcut: copy up to the first 1 from the right, invert the rest)
- Signed numbers: signed-magnitude and 1's complement have **+0 and −0**; 2's complement has one zero
- n-bit 2's complement range **−2ⁿ⁻¹ … 2ⁿ⁻¹−1** (8 bits: −128 … +127); 1's complement / signed magnitude: −127 … +127
- −18 = 11101110; 10000000 = −128; sign extension copies the sign bit

## Fixed and floating point
- Fixed point: point assumed at the right (integers) or left (fractions); 4.4 unsigned max = 15.9375
- Floating point m × rᵉ; **normalized** = mantissa MSB is 1
- IEEE 754 single: 1 + 8 + 23, bias 127; double: 1 + 11 + 52, bias 1023; hidden leading 1
- 5.75 = 40B80000; C1200000 = −10.0

## Codes and error detection
- BCD 8421 (85 = 1000 0101); packed BCD = 2 digits/byte; Excess-3 = BCD + 3 (self-complementing); 2421 self-complementing
- Gray code: one bit changes between successive values; ASCII 7-bit (A = 65, a = 97, 0 = 48, space = 32); EBCDIC 8-bit (IBM); Unicode/UTF-8 1–4 bytes
- Parity detects odd numbers of errors; Hamming: 2ᵖ ≥ m + p + 1 (4 data → 3 check, 8 data → 4); detect d errors: distance d + 1; correct t: 2t + 1
- CRC: divide by a generator polynomial, append the remainder

notes.title: Computer arithmetic – revision sheet
notes.md:
## Addition and subtraction
- 2's complement: A − B = A + B' + 1; **discard** the end carry
- 1's complement: **end-around carry** (add the carry back to the LSB)
- **Overflow** V = Cₙ ⊕ Cₙ₋₁ – only when both operands have the same sign and the result's sign differs; never for opposite signs
- Signed magnitude: same signs → add magnitudes; different signs → subtract smaller from larger, sign of the larger; clear the sign for a zero result
- Unsigned A − B: end carry 1 → A ≥ B
- BCD addition: if the 4-bit sum > 9 or a carry occurs, **add 0110**
- Carry look-ahead: Gᵢ = AᵢBᵢ, Pᵢ = Aᵢ ⊕ Bᵢ, Cᵢ₊₁ = Gᵢ + PᵢCᵢ; ripple adder delay grows with n
- Arithmetic shift left = ×2 (overflow if the sign changes); arithmetic shift right = ÷2 (sign copied)

## Multiplication
- n × n bits → 2n-bit product; shift-and-add: one cycle per multiplier bit (SC = n)
- **Booth** (signed 2's complement): look at Qₙ Qₙ₊₁ (Qₙ₊₁ starts at 0)
  - 10 → subtract M, then ASHR; 01 → add M, then ASHR; 00 / 11 → ASHR only
  - recoding 01110 → +1 0 0 −1 0; worst case: alternating 0101…
- Bit-pair (radix-4) Booth halves the partial products; Wallace tree = carry-save adders; array multiplier n × n AND gates

## Division
- Restoring: subtract; if negative, add the divisor back (quotient bit 0)
- Non-restoring: no restore – next step adds the divisor; final correction if the remainder is negative
- Divide overflow (DVF): upper half of dividend ≥ divisor (e.g. ÷ 0)
- Sign of product/quotient = As ⊕ Bs

## Floating-point arithmetic
- Add/subtract: align (shift the smaller exponent's mantissa right), add, normalize
- Multiply: add exponents (subtract one bias), multiply mantissas, normalize
- Divide: subtract exponents (add the bias), divide mantissas
- Guard bits reduce rounding error

notes.title: Mano's basic computer – revision sheet
notes.md:
## Organization
- Stored program (von Neumann): instructions + data in one memory; PC holds the next instruction's address
- Memory 4096 × 16; instruction = **I (1) | opcode (3) | address (12)**; I = 1 → indirect (one extra read)
- Effective address = address actually used for the operand

| Register | Bits | Use |
|---|---|---|
| DR | 16 | data register |
| AR | 12 | address register (MAR) |
| AC | 16 | accumulator (working area) |
| IR | 16 | instruction register |
| PC | 12 | program counter |
| TR | 16 | temporary register |
| INPR / OUTR | 8 | input / output character |
- Common bus: 16 lines, 7 sources chosen by S₂S₁S₀
- Microoperations: R2 ← R1; P: R2 ← R1 (only when P = 1); selective set = OR, selective clear/mask = AND, selective complement = XOR; shifts: logical, circular, arithmetic

## Instructions (25)
- Memory-reference (opcode 000–110; hex 0–6 direct, 8–E indirect): AND 0, ADD 1, LDA 2, STA 3, BUN 4, BSA 5, ISZ 6
- Register-reference (7xxx): CLA 7800, CLE 7400, CMA 7200, CME 7100, CIR 7080, CIL 7040, INC 7020, SPA 7010, SNA 7008, SZA 7004, SZE 7002, HLT 7001
- I/O (Fxxx): INP F800, OUT F400, SKI F200, SKO F100, ION F080, IOF F040
- Complete instruction set: arithmetic/logic/shift, data transfer, program control/status, I/O

## Timing, instruction cycle, interrupt
- SC (4-bit) + 4 × 16 decoder → T0…T15; 3 × 8 decoder on IR(12–14) → D0…D7
- Fetch: T0 AR ← PC; T1 IR ← M[AR], PC ← PC + 1; T2 decode, AR ← IR(0–11), I ← IR(15); T3 AR ← M[AR] if indirect
- LDA: DR ← M[AR], AC ← DR; STA: M[AR] ← AC; BUN: PC ← AR; **BSA: M[AR] ← PC, PC ← AR + 1**; ISZ: increment, skip if 0
- Flags FGI (input ready), FGO (output ready), IEN (ION/IOF), R (interrupt cycle)
- R ← 1 when IEN·(FGI + FGO) outside T0–T2; interrupt cycle: return address → location 0, PC ← 1, IEN ← 0
- Hardwired control (gates, fast) vs microprogrammed (control memory/ROM, CAR, CDR = pipeline register, easy to change)

notes.md:
## Languages and the assembler
- Machine language (binary/hex) → assembly (mnemonics, labels; machine-dependent; one line ≈ one instruction) → high-level
- Mano's line: **label, instruction, comment (/)**; pseudo-instructions ORG N, END, DEC N, HEX N (directives, not machine code)
- Two-pass assembler: **pass 1** – location counter, address symbol table (labels, literals); **pass 2** – object code using pseudo, MRI, non-MRI and symbol tables, listing
- Two passes are needed for forward references; one-pass assemblers back-patch
- Codes: LDA 500 = 2500, LDA 500 I = A500; ADD = 1xxx; CLA = 7800
- Macro = expanded in-line at assembly time; subroutine = called at run time; cross-assembler = for another processor

## Loops and arithmetic
- Counter = −N, ISZ skips the branch back when it reaches 0; pointer + indirect addressing for arrays
- Subtract: CMA, INC, ADD; OR via De Morgan (CMA, AND, CMA); logical shift: CLE then CIR/CIL
- Multiply by shift-and-add; double precision: low halves, then high halves + E

## Subroutines and I/O
- Call: BSA SUB (return address in SUB's first word); return: BUN SUB I; parameters in AC or after the call; no recursion
- Input: SKI / BUN back / INP; output: SKO / BUN back / OUT (programmed I/O = busy waiting)
- Interrupt service routine: save AC and E, service the device, restore, ION, BUN 0 I
- Pack two characters: CIL × 8 then ADD

notes.md:
## General register organization
- 7 registers on a bus system; SELA/SELB drive two MUXes (ALU inputs), SELD drives a 3 × 8 decoder (destination)
- Control word 14 bits = SELA 3 + SELB 3 + SELD 3 + OPR 5; R1 ← R2 + R3 → SELA = R2, SELB = R3, SELD = R1, OPR = ADD
- ALU status bits: C (carry), S (sign), Z (zero), V (overflow)

## Stack organization
- LIFO; SP = top; 64-word register stack → 6-bit SP, FULL/EMTY flags
- Memory stack growing down: PUSH SP ← SP − 1, M[SP] ← DR; POP DR ← M[SP], SP ← SP + 1; limit registers check overflow/underflow
- Reverse Polish: (A + B) * (C + D) → A B + C D + *; 3 4 * 5 6 * + = 42

## Instruction formats – X = (A + B) * (C + D)
| Format | Instructions |
|---|---|
| Three-address | 3 (short program, long instructions) |
| Two-address | 6 |
| One-address (AC) | 7 |
| Zero-address (stack) | 8 |
- Opcode bits ≥ ⌈log₂ operations⌉ (100 ops → 7 bits); expanding opcode

## Addressing modes (EA = effective address)
| Mode | EA / operand |
|---|---|
| Implied | in the opcode (CMA) |
| Immediate | operand in the instruction (no memory access) |
| Register / register indirect | in register / address in register |
| Direct | address field |
| Indirect | M[address field] (2 memory accesses) |
| Relative | PC + address field |
| Indexed | XR + address field |
| Base register | base + address (relocation) |
| Autoincrement/decrement | register indirect, then ±1 |
- Mano example: PC = 202, address 500, XR = 100 → relative 702, indexed 600

## RISC vs CISC and pipelining
- RISC: few simple instructions, fixed length, load/store, many registers, register windows, hardwired, ~1 cycle, delayed branch (ARM, MIPS, SPARC, RISC-V)
- CISC: many instructions and modes, variable length, memory operands, microprogrammed (x86, VAX)
- Pipeline: k stages, n instructions → k + n − 1 cycles; speed-up nk / (k + n − 1); with s stall cycles per instruction speed-up = k / (1 + s)
- Hazards: structural, data (dependency – forwarding), control/instruction (branches – prediction, delay slots); stalls reduced by forwarding, prediction, out-of-order execution, register renaming

notes.title: I/O organization – revision sheet
notes.md:
## Interface
- Needed because of differences in signals, speed, data format and modes; I/O bus = data + address + control lines
- Commands: control, status, data output, data input; registers chosen by CS, RS1, RS0 (ports A, B, control, status)
- Isolated I/O (separate address space, IN/OUT, I/O read/write lines) vs memory-mapped I/O (I/O registers are memory addresses; all memory instructions work)
- IOP / channel runs its own I/O programs; chips: 8255 PPI, 8251 USART, 8253/54 timer, 8257/8237 DMA, 8259 PIC

## Asynchronous transfer
- Strobe (one line; source- or destination-initiated) – no acknowledgement
- Handshaking (two lines: data valid / data accepted; timeout detects faults): b → a → c → d sequence
- Synchronous transfer uses a common clock (CPU–memory)

## Modes of transfer
1. Programmed I/O – CPU polls the flag (busy waiting)
2. Interrupt-initiated I/O – device interrupts when ready
3. DMA – BR/BG; address, word-count and control registers; burst vs cycle stealing; interrupt when the count reaches 0

## Priority interrupt
- Software polling; daisy chain (nearest device highest; PI/PO; vector on the bus); parallel (interrupt register + mask register + priority encoder)
- Vectored vs non-vectored; maskable vs non-maskable; internal (trap), external, software interrupts
- 8085: TRAP (24H, NMI) > RST 7.5 (3CH) > RST 6.5 (34H) > RST 5.5 (2CH) > INTR; interrupt latency = request → start of ISR

## Serial communication
- Asynchronous: start bit 0, 5–8 data bits, optional parity, 1–2 stop bits; 10 char/s × 11 bits = 110 baud; UART
- Synchronous: blocks with sync characters, no start/stop bits per character
